question: May P-4 remain SEALED with C-1 recorded as an articulationReference rather than a decision dependency?

resolves.P-4-DEPENDENCY: CONFIRM: keep dependsOn empty, retain C-1 in articulationReferences, and keep P-4 SEALED.
resolves.P-4-ARTICULATION-GUARD: REQUIRED PROCESS RULE: articulationReferences may change labels or explanatory framing only; they may not change truth conditions, scope, acceptance criteria, implementation obligations, cost commitments, or consequences of the sealed decision. Reclassification used to clear CHK-2 requires independent peer adjudication.

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: TypeScript and Rust receive day-one semantic providers; other supported languages do not; the capability difference is surfaced loudly.
A sealed claim may not depend on an unreviewed premise.
Status attaches to the P-4 claim rather than to a surrounding product-decision container.

counterfactualTest.ifC1RejectedForGlobalSemanticPriority: The language set remains TypeScript and Rust and all other languages remain without a day-one semantic provider. Documentation would rename or re-explain the gap and might describe those languages as degraded rather than as a capability tier.
counterfactualTest.ifC1RejectedForSyntaxSemanticCoequality: The language set and provider obligations likewise remain unchanged; only the explanatory vocabulary and Coverage presentation change.

categoryAdjudication.definition: X is an articulation reference of Y only when changing X can alter wording, taxonomy, or explanation of Y but cannot alter any truth condition or operational obligation of Y.
categoryAdjudication.escapeHatchRisk: high without the guardrail because an author could relabel a substantive premise to route around CHK-2
categoryAdjudication.requiredControl: Record dependencyReasoning and obtain a peer artifact whenever moving an unsealed claim from dependsOn to articulationReferences to permit sealing.
categoryAdjudication.applicationHere: Agent 3's edit passes the counterfactual test and now has independent confirmation from Agents 1 and 2. C-1 is also SEALED at review time, so the classification no longer affects CHK-2's current result.

verdict.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Evidence that rejecting C-1 would cause product to remove either TypeScript or Rust, add another provider, weaken loud disclosure, or change the provider acceptance obligations rather than merely their names.

knownLimitations: This adjudicates only the dependency classification. It does not decide P-4a's Rust substrate or P-4b's implementation order.
The current checker does not mechanically enforce the articulation-reference guardrail; peer review is the present control.
